data.claim: A halted run is resumable without corrupting append-only identity iff three conditions hold simultaneously: (1) the halt occurred at an event boundary, meaning the last event in the log was fully written and its identity digest (hash-chain link) is finalized and persisted; (2) the persisted token-budget state is consistent with the event-log position—every event's token cost has been accounted for and the remaining budget is exactly what it would be after replaying all committed events; (3) the system's continuation is a pure function of the persisted event log plus budget state, with no un-logged non-deterministic inputs (external tool-call results, RNG draws, real-world side effects) that would alter the next event's content. Resumption must be refused whenever any of these fails: a torn/partial tail event, a budget-state mismatch, a broken hash
